title: Opposition discusses Supreme Court retirement age proposal - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 23 (Daily Mirror) - A special discussion among opposition party leaders on the government’s proposal to extend the retirement age of Supreme Court judges is currently being held at the Opposition Leader’s Office in Colombo.

Former President Ranil Wickremesinghe, Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa, Sarva Jana Balaya Leader Dilith Jayaweera, Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna National Organizer Namal Rajapaksa, former Prime Minister Dinesh Gunawardena and several other opposition representatives have arrived to participate in the meeting.

The discussion was convened at the invitation of Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa to discuss the proposed amendment regarding the retirement age of Supreme Court judges and other related matters.

title: Two Chinese nationals arrested at BIA over alleged Port City gang clash killing - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By T.K.G Kapila

Two Chinese nationals accused of killing a member of a rival gang during a clash between two Chinese groups at the Colombo Port City were arrested at the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) while attempting to flee the country.

The suspects, aged 34 and 38, were arrested by officers of the Airport Criminal Investigation Department (CID) at the departure terminal on Thursday (23) afternoon and were later handed over to the Colombo Port Police.

The two men had arrived at the Katunayake Airport at around 4.30 p.m. to board Air India flight AI-2275 bound for Singapore via Mumbai, India. They had reportedly purchased air tickets with Singapore as their final destination.

Airport CID officers, acting on intelligence received regarding their attempted departure, carried out surveillance operations at the departure terminal and arrested the two suspects.

Police said further investigations are being conducted by the Colombo Port Police.

title: Prof. Peiris to establish legal research trust for Colombo University and Law College - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 23 (Daily Mirror) - Professor G.L. Peiris has announced plans to establish a Trust Fund to support legal research and academic initiatives at the Faculty of Law, University of Colombo, and the Sri Lanka Law College.

Making the announcement at the launch of the Sinhala legal journal “Nitiya” at the Sri Lanka Law College recently, Prof. Peiris said the fund would be created using the royalties he receives as the author of more than ten books on Sri Lankan laws and legal systems.

He said the proposed Trustees of the fund would include the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Colombo, the Principal of the Sri Lanka Law College, and the Dean of the Faculty of Law at the University of Colombo.

The launch event was attended by Attorney General Parinda Ranasinghe, PC, President of the Bar Association of Sri Lanka Rajeev Amarasuriya, and Principal of the Sri Lanka Law College Prasantha Lal de Alwis, PC.

Speaking at the event, Prof. Peiris praised the initiatives taken by Mr. de Alwis to expand the activities of the Law College beyond traditional classroom teaching by introducing various literary, cultural and academic programmes.

He said these efforts had brought renewed energy to an institution with a long and respected history.

Prof. Peiris also highlighted the importance of Nitiya, a Sinhala legal journal first published in 1958, which was revived in 2024 after a period of interruption.

He said the journal provides a platform for analytical writing on legal issues, including emerging fields such as Artificial Intelligence, while encouraging informed criticism of judicial decisions and contributions to the legislative process.

He highlighted that institutions such as the Sri Lanka Law College should play a key role in promoting legal research and academic discussions on evolving areas of law.

title: Tax burden unfair despite government revenue claims: Namal - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 23 (Daily Mirror) - Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organizer Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa has accused the government of imposing an unfair tax burden on the public despite claiming to have large amounts of revenue.

Addressing a meeting in Udahamulla yesterday (July 22), he said that although President Anura Kumara Dissanayake had said that the government had “crores of rupees”, there was no sufficient investment or benefit provided to the people in return for the taxes they pay.

“The President proudly says, ‘We have crores of rupees.’ However, there is no investment in the country that is fair considering the amount of tax paid by the people,” he said.

Namal said the country was currently facing severe economic difficulties, with the cost of living increasing daily while taxes were being increased without proper consideration.

He alleged that the public was being forced to cover financial losses caused by government failures.

“If there is any loss or theft within the government, the people are taxed to recover those losses,” he claimed.

Commenting on recent increases in electricity tariffs and fuel prices, Rajapaksa linked them to issues including the import of substandard coal and questioned whether ordinary citizens should bear the cost of such problems.

title: Labour Department suspends EPF services on July 30 and 31 - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 23 (Daily Mirror) - The Labour Department has announced that public services related to the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) Database and Digital EPF system will be unavailable on July 30 and 31, 2026, due to essential maintenance work on its computer system.

Commissioner General of Labour said H.M.D.N.K. Wataliyadda said the temporary suspension will affect the Department's head office as well as all zonal, district and sub-district labour offices. Services including EPF benefit payments and registrations will not be available during the two-day period.

The Department also said that individuals who had already booked appointments for services on those dates may visit the relevant labour office on any other working day within one month to obtain the required services.

title: Former State Minister’s son remanded over Rs. 20Mn robbery case - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 23 (Daily Mirror) - Former State Minister Shantha Bandara's son, Anuda Bandara, was today remanded until July 27 over his alleged involvement in the robbery of Rs. 20 million belonging to a Chinese national.

Fort Magistrate Pasan Amarasena issued the remand order after the suspect was detained and questioned for 24 hours by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID).

CID officers informed the court that investigations are being conducted into the suspect’s telephone and bank records, along with possible cryptocurrency transactions believed to be linked to the incident.

The first suspect in the case was identified by a witness during an identification parade held at the Magistrate’s Court premises earlier today.

Further investigations are being conducted by the CID.

title: Gun discovered after clash between Chinese nationals at Port City - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 23 (Daily Mirror) - A pistol and a communication device have been found in a vehicle linked to a clash between two groups of Chinese nationals at the Colombo Port City, police said.

According to police, two Chinese nationals were injured in the clash and admitted to a private hospital for treatment.

Police further said that another Chinese national, who is believed to have been injured during the altercation, was allegedly taken away from the scene by members of the opposing group involved in the dispute.

A search of a vehicle found at the scene led to the discovery of the pistol and the communication device.

The Colombo Harbour Police are conducting further investigations into the incident.

title: Five soldiers killed in southern Thailand checkpoint attack
summary: Five Thai paramilitary soldiers have been killed and six civilians wounded in an attack on a security checkpoint in the country’s rebel-hit south, according to the army.

title: Vehicle imports drop remarkably: Minister - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Ajith Siriwardana and Yohan Perera

Colombo, July 23 (Daily Mirror) - Deputy Minister of Finance Anil Jayantha Fernando said today that vehicle imports have reduced remarkably after the imposition of the 50 percent surcharge on vehicle imports.

The Minister told Parliament that the average value of Letters of Credit (LCs) opened for vehilce imports during the first six months of this year stands at USD 3.5 million.

He said Letters of Credit (LCs) have been opened only at USD 1.8 million on July 20 and USD 1.9 million on July 21.

It was earlier revealed that Letters of Credit (LCs) valued at USD 23.71 million had been opened on May 15 on the cutoff date of the imposition of the surcharge.

title: CAA warns private hospitals against overcharging for FBC, Dengue tests - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 23 (Daily Mirror) - The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) has reminded private hospitals and laboratories that maximum charges remain in force for certain medical laboratory tests, following reports that a private hospital in Jaffna had allegedly charged above the approved fee for a Full Blood Count (FBC) test.

In a statement, the CAA said that under Order No. 67 issued in terms of Section 20(5) of the Consumer Affairs Authority Act, No. 09 of 2003, the maximum charge for a Full Blood Count (FBC) test, including the report, is Rs. 400, while the maximum charge for a Dengue NS1 Antigen test, including the report, is Rs. 1,200.

The authority noted that the order has been in effect since July 29, 2020, following its publication in the Extraordinary Gazette No. 2186/17.

The clarification was issued after complaints emerged regarding a private healthcare institution in Jaffna allegedly charging more than the prescribed fee for an FBC test.

The CAA urged the public to remain vigilant when obtaining laboratory services from private hospitals and medical laboratories and advised patients to request an official bill or receipt for all payments made.

Consumers who are charged above the approved maximum fee can lodge complaints with the CAA through its 1977 hotline.

The authority said complaints should be accompanied by receipts and any other relevant evidence to facilitate investigations

title: Selfie attempt at Knuckles Waterfall claims lives of two schoolboys - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Shane Seneviratne

Colombo, July 23 (Daily Mirror) - Two schoolboys lost their lives after attempting to take selfies from the top of the Jodu Ella waterfall in the Knuckles forest range yesterday.

The victims, identified as B. Saljith and K. Delon, were Grade Nine students of the Knuckles Tamil Maha Vidyalaya and residents of Knuckles Estate in Thawalantenna.

According to police investigations, the two boys were among a group of five schoolboys who had visited the scenic Jodu Ella waterfall. While standing on a boulder at the top of the falls to take selfies, they reportedly slipped and plunged into the waterfall.

One of the boys died at the scene, while the other succumbed to his injuries while being transferred from the Madolkele Divisional Hospital to the National Hospital, Kandy.

The Panvila Police have launched an investigation into the fatal incident.

title: Gotabaya Rajapaksa appears before Court of Appeal over arrest petition - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 23 (Daily Mirror) - Former President Gotabaya Rajapaksa appeared before the Court of Appeal today (23) to observe proceedings related to a writ petition he has filed seeking an order preventing his arrest and detention.

The Court of Appeal is scheduled to take up the petition for further consideration today. The matter was previously considered for the fourth consecutive day on July 9 before a two-judge bench comprising Court of Appeal President Justice Rohantha Abeysooriya and Justice Sarath Dissanayake. Following the proceedings, further hearings were postponed to today.

title: Beware of fake police officers demanding bank details on WhatsApp - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 23 (Daily Mirror) - The Sri Lanka Police have issued an urgent public warning over a surge in financial scams involving fraudsters impersonating police officers and other government officials to steal money and sensitive banking information.

Police said criminals are using stolen or fabricated photographs to create fake profiles on messaging platforms such as WhatsApp and Telegram to deceive members of the public. Despite previous arrests and awareness campaigns, police said people continue to fall victim to the scams.

According to police, victims are contacted by individuals falsely claiming to represent the Central Bank of Sri Lanka, the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), or other police investigation units. The callers typically allege that the victim's National Identity Card has been used in fraudulent activities or that their bank accounts are linked to money laundering and other criminal offences.

To make their claims appear genuine, the scammers send forged police identity cards, official-looking documents and badges through social media while threatening victims with legal action and offering to help resolve the purported investigations.

Police said the fraudsters then persuade victims to reveal confidential information, including One-Time Passwords (OTPs), banking credentials and PINs. In some cases, victims are pressured into transferring money to unfamiliar bank accounts or purchasing and transferring cryptocurrency, including USDT.

The Police stressed that no government institution or private organisation will ever request OTPs, CVV numbers, bank passwords or other confidential banking details over the telephone or through social media.

They also clarified that neither the Sri Lanka Police, the CID nor the Central Bank of Sri Lanka conduct official investigations through personal WhatsApp accounts or ask members of the public to deposit money into personal bank accounts. Official police communications are issued only through formal written notices or by officers carrying out official duties in person.

The public has been advised not to click on suspicious web links, download files from unknown sources or scan unverified QR codes. Anyone who receives forged documents bearing government logos has been urged to report the matter to the nearest police station immediately.

Police further reminded the public that no fees are charged for criminal investigations. Victims or anyone targeted by such scams can contact the Computer Crime Investigation Division on 011-2300756 or 071-8592918 and 071-8591765, or visit the CID in person to lodge a complaint.

title: Police Officer’s house targeted in shooting in Beliatta - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 23 (Daily Mirror) - A house belonging to a police officer in the Walawala area of Beliatta came under gunfire, police said.

The officer, who is attached to the Dickwella Police, was not reported injured in the incident.

Police said that around five shots were fired at the gate of the house. No casualties have been reported.

An investigation has been launched to identify the suspects and determine the motive behind the shooting.
